definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese storehouse, typically a thick-walled building made of earth or plaster, designed to protect valuables, food, and goods from fire and theft. Also used more broadly for any storage building.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{蔵|くら}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{改装|かいそう}→改装：09682_kaisou⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦カフェ→カフェ：06767_kafe⟧にした。
examples.english: They renovated an old storehouse into a café.

examples.japanese: {蔵|くら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{貴重|きちょう}→貴重：00223_kichou⟧な⟦{掛|か}け{軸|じく}→掛け軸：06122_kakejiku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}つかった→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧。
examples.english: A valuable hanging scroll was found inside the storehouse.

examples.english: This sake brewery is a long-established business dating from the Edo period, still making sake using traditional methods.

notes:
USAGE:
Traditional {蔵|くら} are iconic elements of Japanese architecture, especially in merchant towns. Many have been repurposed as restaurants, galleries, and museums. The word also appears in many compounds related to storage and production.

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{酒蔵|さかぐら}→酒蔵：08633_sakagura⟧: sake brewery/cellar
- {米蔵|こめぐら}: rice storehouse
- {蔵元|くらもと}: sake brewery owner/operator
- ⟦{蔵書|ぞうしょ}→蔵書：15479_zousho⟧: book collection, library holdings
- ⟦{土蔵|どぞう}→土蔵：15634_dozou⟧: earthen storehouse
- ⟦お{蔵入|くらい}り→お蔵入り：23210_okurairi⟧: being shelved, put into storage (figuratively: a project being abandoned)
